children: On the final trading session of the truncated week, the benchmark Nifty 50 witnessed heightened volatility amid persistent selling pressure. The index opened nearly 90 points lower and extended its losses in the first 10 minutes of trade.
While an initial recovery during the first hour helped limit the decline, the index remained in consolidation mode through the session and eventually ended Friday 155 points lower.

The index appears to have encountered resistance near the crucial 25,200 mark, which coincides with the previous opening gap-down level of March 2, 2026. This comes after the sharp rally witnessed in the previous week.

Among Nifty constituents, Eicher Motors and Hindustan Unilever were the top gainers, lending some support to the benchmark. On the other hand, Shriram Finance and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles were among the biggest laggards.

Sectoral performance remained largely negative, with all sectoral indices ending in the red, barring Nifty MidSmall IT & Telecom. Nifty Cement, Nifty Realty and Nifty Auto emerged as the worst-performing indices.
The broader markets, however, displayed relative resilience. Both the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 outperformed the benchmark Nifty 50, although they too ended the session lower.
What lies ahead for the Nifty?

Indian equities are likely to witness some consolidation in the near term, although the broader outlook remains positive, with the market retaining a gradual upward bias. The Q2FY27 earnings season has concluded on a strong note, with corporate performance largely exceeding expectations and improving earnings visibility.

Record foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows have provided additional support to domestic equities. Meanwhile, the recent correction in global AI stocks has also redirected some investor interest towards Indian markets.

However, certain domestic and global factors could temper the pace of gains. Retail inflation rising above the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance limit and crude oil prices moving back above $95.4 per barrel could weigh on investor sentiment in the near term.
While these headwinds may limit near-term upside, strong corporate earnings and continued FII participation remain supportive of the broader market outlook.

Globally, Nvidia's Q3 results, scheduled for Wednesday, will be a key event for investors. The company's performance and management commentary could influence global technology sentiment and provide further cues on whether the ongoing rotation away from AI-heavy stocks towards markets such as India will continue.
The US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes, also due on Wednesday, will be closely tracked for indications of the Federal Reserve's policy trajectory ahead of its December meeting.
Other important economic releases include US retail sales, UK CPI inflation, China's industrial production and flash November PMI readings.
On the domestic earnings front, investors will track Q2FY27 results from Ashok Leyland, Kaynes Technology India and Hero Motors, among others, over the weekend.
Nagaraj Shetti of HDFC Securities expects the current weakness to subside by next week, with the 24,800-24,700 zone acting as an immediate support area.
On the upside, resistance is placed around 25,400. A sustained move above this level could pave the way for the next leg of the market's upward move.

Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities said the 24,900-24,850 zone is expected to act as an important support area for the index. A decisive break below 24,850 could accelerate selling pressure and drag the index towards the 24,600 mark in the near term.

On the upside, the recent swing high of 25,424 remains the immediate resistance. A sustained move above this level would indicate renewed buying momentum and strengthen the prospects of the prevailing uptrend continuing.
Hitesh Rathi of Angel One said the 25,050-25,000 band would act as immediate support, followed by a stronger support zone at 24,800-24,700.
On the upside, the 25,260-25,350 range is likely to act as an immediate hurdle, followed by a stronger resistance zone at 25,400-25,500.

title: Nifty Outlook for November 16: Index may see near-term consolidation after Friday's fall; key levels to watch
